ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 3×3 square grid; the middle cell is marked with a question mark, indicating that the number in the middle cell is required; the other eight cells are blank. The problem states that the sum formed by the nine integers is 500, and that the numbers in any two adjacent cells sharing a common side differ by exactly 1. Reasoning: Let the number in the middle cell be c. The four side-adjacent cells sharing a side with the center cell must all be c+1 or c-1, so the absolute value of the difference between each of them and c is 1. The four corner cells require two steps to reach from the center cell, and the value changes by 1 at each step, so the absolute value of the difference between each corner cell and c is at most 2. Therefore, the absolute value of the difference between the sum of the nine numbers and 9c is at most 4·1+4·2=12, that is, |500-9c|≤12. Thus 488≤9c≤512, so c can only be the integer 55 or 56. Then use parity: Adjacent cells differ by 1, so adjacent cells have opposite parity. Taking the center cell as the reference, the center cell and the four corner cells have an even grid distance to the center, so their parity is the same as c; the four side-adjacent cells have an odd distance to the center, so their parity is opposite to c. Therefore, the parity of the sum of the nine numbers is the same as the parity of c. The sum 500 is even, so c must be even. Among 55 and 56, only 56 is even.

raw_record.question_text: Nine whole numbers were written into the cells of a $3 \times 3$ table. The sum of these nine numbers is 500. We know that the numbers in two adjacent cells (with a common sideline) differ by exactly 1. Which number is in the middle cell?

method.method_draft: Use a distance-from-center bound plus a parity argument. Read the image as a 3x3 grid with one middle cell, four side-neighbor cells, and four corner cells. From the text, let the middle number be c, the total sum be 500, and every side-adjacent pair differ by exactly 1. The four side-neighbors of the center must be c±1, and each corner is two grid-steps from the center, so it can differ from c by at most 2. Therefore the total differs from 9c by at most 4·1+4·2=12, so |500-9c|≤12, giving c∈{55,56}. Now use checkerboard parity: cells at even grid distance from the center, namely the center and four corners, have the same parity as c; the four side-neighbors have the opposite parity. Thus the parity of the whole sum is the parity of c. Since 500 is even, c is even, so c=56.

推理：设中间格的数为 c。与中心格共边的四个边邻格都必须是 c+1 或 c-1，因此每个与 c 的差的绝对值为 1。四个角格距离中心格需要走两步，每走一步数值变化 1，所以每个角格与 c 的差的绝对值最多为 2。因此，九个数的总和与 9c 的差的绝对值最多为 4·1+4·2=12，即 |500-9c|≤12。于是 488≤9c≤512，所以 c 只能是整数 55 或 56。

再用奇偶性：相邻格相差 1，所以相邻格奇偶性相反。以中心格为基准，中心格和四个角格到中心的网格距离为偶数，奇偶性与 c 相同；四个边邻格到中心距离为奇数，奇偶性与 c 相反。因此九个数总和的奇偶性与 c 的奇偶性相同。总和 500 是偶数，所以 c 必须是偶数。在 55 和 56 中，只有 56 是偶数。
